subject: Urgent capacity escalation: Hosted throttling -> decision on Dedicated / Private

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (capacity options)

Hi Jacob — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment after the demo:

- Observed workload: batch requests to summarization and a couple low-latency chat routes (~120–220 qps spikes)
- Your stated priorities: predictable latency for user-facing flows, data isolation requirements for HIPAA scope, and cost controls

Given the workload and compliance note, we flagged three deployment modes for discussion:
1) Hosted API: fastest onboarding, no infra work from FastStream; good for early prod but less isolation and subject to shared-capacity throttling
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool with SLA-backed throughput and predictable cost; ~24–72 hour onboarding if capacity available
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation and KMS controls; procurement + network setup typically 2–4 weeks

Next steps I proposed on the call:
- I will follow up with an initial incident-driven assessment and a short capacity recommendation (this email)
- Vivek to share a temporary mitigation playbook for immediate spikes
- If FastStream wants to accelerate, we can prepare a Dedicated proposal and an expedited onboarding timeline

Please confirm if you want us to prepare a Dedicated quote now (we can turn up a reserved pool within 48–72 hrs on an expedited path) or if you prefer to start Private onboarding planning.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Marissa — appreciate the recap. Headline: we had a production incident overnight (2:14–2:19am PDT) where our user-facing summarization route saw a sudden 5x spike and calls started getting 429s from Redwood hosted endpoints. Impact: brief UX errors for paying customers and an internal pager.

We need an accelerated plan. Our CTO Selena is looped in. Two asks from our side: 
1) Immediate mitigation — can Redwood guarantee a reserved pool or emergency uplift while we decide?
2) Short-term decision: if Dedicated gives predictable throughput and strict tenancy, that’s likely what we want. We still want to evaluate Private (VPC) for HIPAA later, but this incident pushes Dedicated higher on the priority list.

We need pricing and an estimate for time-to-onboard. Also, please include any temporary route-level throttling or caching suggestions we can implement today.

Jacob
Director of Product, FastStream AI

Adding technical recommendations and options — copied from incident triage notes.

Immediate (within 1–4 hours):
- Temporary routing: create an emergency reserved pool (if capacity available in the cluster) and route FastStream traffic there using a policy with higher token limits. This is reversible and preserves Hosted routing for other customers.
- Prefix caching: enable prefix/KV cache on their summarization model and increase cache TTLs for common user prompts. Vivek can push conservative cache rules to reduce peak token cost.
- Per-route throttles: relax soft-limits but enforce a short-term per-API-key token cap to avoid uncontrolled spikes.

Dedicated (recommended near-term):
- Suggested config: 2x high-memory GPU nodes (equivalent of 80K token/s sustained), dedicated KV cache, and reserved pre-warmed KV slots.
- Onboarding ETA: expedited path 48–72 hours (we allocate existing pool and prioritize networking/ingress), normal path 5–7 business days if new capacity must be provisioned.
- Cost delta: ~2.8x the current hosted per-token baseline for 24/7 reserved pool; we’ll send formal quote.

Private (VPC) (longer-term):
- Timeline: 2–3 weeks (legal, network peering, KMS), good for HIPAA and audit controls.

I’ve attached a short incident log extract and a proposed Dedicated config template. Neha — we may need an emergency two-week SOW to cover expedited provisioning and cancelable reserved billing; can you prepare a draft we can send to FastStream?

Regards,
Rishi
Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

- Redwood: Neha to share SOW and draft redlines; Rishi and Vivek to begin provisioning plan once APPROVE received

Jacob — happy to hop on a short call to walk through the SOW and timelines this afternoon. Please reply with preferred next step.
